text: You look worried. Is everything OK?
My phone has no battery. Can I borrow your charger?
Sure, you can. It's in my bag. But you can't use it on the court.
No problem, I can wait in the hall. Sorry, I don't understand one thing. Why not on the court?
Camp rule. No phones on the court. Can you give it back after practice?
Of course. Thank you. Can I help you with anything?
Actually, yes. Can you carry the balls to court B?
Yes, I can. That is easy. I can carry all of them.
I can play basketball and I can swim.
Can I borrow your charger, please?
Sorry, I don't understand. Can you speak more slowly?

Hi, it's Tyler. People ask me what I can do, so here is the honest answer. I can play basketball, of course. I can swim, but not very well. I can cook two things: eggs and pasta. That's all. I can't drive yet, because I am sixteen and here you need to be sixteen and a half. And I can't speak another language. I understand a little Spanish, but I can't have a conversation. Not yet. What about you? What can you do?

Good morning, everybody. Three quick rules for this week. One: you can use your phone in the hall, but you can't use it on the court. Two: you can borrow a ball from the box, but please put it back after practice. Three: if you don't understand an instruction, you can always ask me again. That is not a problem. It is never a problem. Can everybody hear me at the back? Good. Let's start.
Bruno's phone has no battery before the game. He asks a friend for a charger. The friend says he can borrow it. Bruno charges the phone in the hall. He gives the charger back after practice.
